newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed slightly lower against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Thursday in mixed trading, dealers said.
"Trading was mixed and balanced today with slightly more conversions of shekels into dollars," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
He attributed the shekel's decline to several big deals made by the business sector in which dollars were purchased.
The trader said the basket rose mildly, making it unnecessary for the Bank of Israel to intervene.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to support the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for three months.

Figures published on Thursday by the Central Bureau of Statistics show that during the first four months of 1997 the dollar rose by 4.8 percent against the shekel. In March alone the U.S. currency gained 1.4 percent against the shekel.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4100 shekels against 3.4070 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6804 shekels against 3.6788 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6824 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.6877 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.9744 shekels compared with 1.9726 on Wednesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4100 shekels.
